summary: Tested new 12-agent PHI pipeline: /api/health, /api/settings/llm (GET+POST, api_key not leaked), intake with study1.zip, /handle pipeline, agent-trace, and results endpoint. 5/8 tests pass. Two critical bugs found: (1) /handle never extracts dataset column headers, so Schema agent sees only filenames and Judge invents/omits columns (SSN and email columns from patients.csv are missing from decisions entirely because the data_dictionary only listed a subset). (2) Backend uvicorn --reload watches tests/ dir; hot-reload during test runs terminates in-flight background pipeline workers leaving sessions stuck in 'anonymizing'. Frontend /studies/new renders with zip-drop-zone and manifest-spec-panel data-testids.

critical.issue: Pipeline never reads dataset column headers. FileArtifact.columns is populated only by pipeline.ingest_file() which is called by /api/sessions/{sid}/run, NOT by /handle. Result: phi_core/agents/specialists.py Schema.run() reads f.get('columns', []) which is always []; the LLM ends up 'inferring' columns from filename+Lexicon dictionary. With the spec fixture (patients.csv has columns patient_name,dob,ssn,mrn,phone,email,notes but data_dictionary/columns.csv only lists patient_name and ssn), Judge produced 5 decisions with hallucinated names ('medical_record_number','phone_number') and SILENTLY DROPPED ssn and email. Direct-identifier expectations in the spec (ssn=drop) cannot be verified. FIX: in server.py session_handle worker, run pipeline.ingest_file() on each dataset file (or a headers-only variant) before calling run_agent_pipeline() so art.columns is populated. Also propagate art.columns onto the session.files dict passed to run_agent_pipeline.

After resolutions posted, resume worker starts (status='anonymizing') but never completes and audit/ledger/herald remain {}. Root cause during tests: uvicorn --reload observed changes to /app/backend/tests/*.py and restarted the process mid-worker. In production this is triggered any time a code edit happens during an in-flight review resume. Two fixes: (a) exclude tests/ from watch (uvicorn --reload-exclude 'tests/*'); (b) persist worker state and be resumable, OR at minimum surface a status='failed' if the resume aborts. Currently the session is silently stuck with no error field.

minor.issue: When Sentinel doesn't approve within ITERATION_CAP the last decisions set is kept and human_needed forced True, but sentinel_last is only the FINAL sentinel reply; the intermediate feedback prior_feedback is lost from the DB (only summarized inline in Judge prompt). Consider persisting per-iteration sentinel results in agent_log for debugging.
When f['columns'] is empty, agent silently substitutes filename as a 'column'. Should raise / return empty columns so orchestrator can fail loudly instead of hallucinating downstream.
Does not return the 'status' or 'error' fields, so frontend must call /api/sessions/{sid} in parallel to know if pipeline is complete vs awaiting_human_review vs failed.

action_items: Fix /handle to ingest dataset column headers before running the agent pipeline (call pipeline.ingest_file or a headers-only extractor and set art.columns). Without this fix, downstream Schema/Judge/Sentinel decisions are unreliable and the spec's direct-identifier expectations (ssn=drop, email in categories) cannot be met.
Configure uvicorn to not reload on tests/ file changes (add --reload-exclude 'tests/*' or move tests outside the watched dir). This blocks CI-style testing today.
Make /api/sessions/{sid}/human-review worker fail loud on exception (write status='failed' and error message; currently only writes status='anonymizing' on entry, never on exit).

Confirm dataset export produces empty cells for 'drop', 4-digit years for 'year_only', hex tokens for 'pseudonymize' - could NOT be validated end-to-end because pipeline never reached 'complete' after human-review due to reload issue.
OPTIONAL: Add per-iteration sentinel snapshots to agent_log for debugging Judge<->Sentinel loops.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py session_handle: session.files are passed directly to run_agent_pipeline, but files stored by /intake have columns=[] and sha256='' for anything after intake never having been ingested. Either ingest during intake or ingest during handle.
phi_core/agents/specialists.py Schema.run: silently proceeds when headers list is empty; downstream Judge is then forced to guess column names from Lexicon and Instrument only.

server.py session_human_review: exec_out/audit/scout/ledger/herald all executed but if any raises, only status='failed' is set - but the initial 'anonymizing' state has NO retry semantics; a mid-flight kill leaves the session unrecoverable.

orchestrator.py L80-83: if s.get('verdict') != 'approved' after cap, human_needed is forced True but approved_decisions may still contain non-human_review actions the operator won't get to review; UI needs to distinguish between 'human_review' items and Sentinel-rejected items.

phi_core/agents/base.py: agent_log writes are per-agent and lack a rollup; the /agent-trace endpoint is fine but there is no way to know which iteration a message belongs to (iteration index isn't in AgentMessage).
seed_data_creation: Used /root/fixtures/study1.zip (present). Created ~2 sessions during test runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The /intake -> /handle -> agent-trace flow works up to Judge<->Sentinel producing decisions. Two blockers before end-to-end can be re-verified: (1) Schema agent receives empty columns because /handle doesn't extract CSV headers - fix by calling pipeline.ingest_file (or a headers-only helper) on each dataset in the /handle worker before invoking run_agent_pipeline. (2) uvicorn --reload interferes with long-running background workers when any /app/backend file changes; add --reload-exclude 'tests/*' or run tests from outside the watched tree. After the /handle header-extraction fix, direct-identifier expectations should be tested against a session whose data_dictionary reflects ALL columns in the dataset - the current fixture data_dictionary/columns.csv only lists 2 of 7 columns, which is realistic but currently causes Judge to omit the un-dictionaried columns. The spec test at test_results_decisions expects ssn to appear as a decision with action='drop'; this requires Schema to actually see 'ssn' as a header. Frontend /studies/{sid} agent-panel not verified this iteration since no completed happy-path session exists.
rca of the issue: PRIMARY BUG: FileArtifact.columns is set only in phi_core/pipeline.py::ingest_file (invoked by legacy /run endpoint). The new /handle endpoint routes past that path, so Schema.run reads f.get('columns', [])=[] and returns a stub with only the filename. Judge then relies solely on Lexicon (data_dictionary) columns and Instrument (consent PDF text) to name columns, producing decisions like 'medical_record_number' and 'phone_number' that do not match real CSV headers, and silently dropping columns absent from the dictionary (ssn, email in the study1.zip fixture). Reproduction: POST /api/sessions/{sid}/intake with study1.zip, then GET /api/sessions/{sid} - files[dataset].columns==[]. Then POST /api/sessions/{sid}/handle and GET /api/sessions/{sid}/results - decisions[].column values do not intersect the real headers. Fix: in server.py::session_handle worker (before run_agent_pipeline), iterate session.files where kind=='dataset' and populate columns from disk via existing readers.read_csv_columns / read_xlsx_columns, then persist to session.files.
